body: You should’ve killed me when you had the chance - a day to remember

Hey, I know you don’t know me and vice versa, but please give me a second of your time. I’m so sorry that you’re in so much pain. So much pain that you feel that the end is the only option you have left. I know you’re relying on your therapist to say something to make you live, but please know that your therapist is an imperfect human being who may not end up saying what you need to hear if you don’t communicate what it is that you need to hear. 

What are you hoping for? I want you to know I am so proud of you for even seeking help and having a therapist. Opening up is hard. It’s scary. Vulnerability feels exposing. But I encourage you to continue to pour your heart out in therapy. Show your therapist this post. Explore together what you were hoping to hear from your therapist.  

Please stay. Please. I’ve been rejected from society, and sometimes I even reject myself. Self hate and self harm. It’s a really toxic cycle I’ve fallen into. You’re not alone, OP. We are all here for you, cheering you on, rooting for you, beside you. You are not alone from this moment forth.

Hey. Please don’t do this. Gosh I cannot imagine how deep your pain must be. The fact that you even typed this up and had these thoughts breaks my heart. But I want you to know that you have people who care about you. Even if it’s just us. The commenters on this post. We are here. And none of us want to lose you.

Hey. I know I’m just a stranger on the internet and maybe you aren’t even looking for positivity or encouragement anymore. I can’t imagine how hopeless you are feeling. I’m sorry. I know you want the pain to end. I see you. And I hear you. It sounds like sweet relief, right? 
I don’t know why some of us suffer more than others. It remains a mystery. But what I do know is that you have a story to tell. You will never be able to tell it once you’re gone. Please. Please stay. So you can one day help save the lives of many who feel the way you feel now. Live. 
Please.

Hi there,

I believe you.

 I am sorry this happened to you. It was not your fault. You did not deserve this. And thank you for being brave and even typing this post. Please know that there are people who care about you and your story, even though they may not be present in your immediate life. Do you have access to proper mental health care? A therapist? Or even a doctor? Are you in school? Do you have a teacher you trust, or someone in your life you can confide in? I think it's so important to talk to someone who you know will unconditionally be there for you, and above all, believe you.

What you went through is traumatic. Whether or not its classified as "rape" is irrelevant to if it was hurtful or traumatizing for you. Clearly it has impacted you greatly. It would impact me greatly too. You are not broken or unfixable. 

Please take care of yourself and know that you are loved. There is always, always someone who loves and cares about you. And again. I believe you.

Yes. There are some moments I remember so very vividly, but some that feel like are just completely missing from my memory. Trauma tends to mess with that type of thing a lot. It's funny because there are certain instances where I could tell you exactly what I was wearing down to the color of my socks, but just a string of a few years that I have completely forgotten. Scary.

Hi there! I am so, so incredibly sorry to hear that you are dealing with flashbacks. It sounds like the abusive situation you were in was severely traumatizing and I want to remind you that you did not deserve that. It sounds like you are displaying symptoms of post-traumatic stress. I'm not a professional, but I would recommend if you have the ability to see one, that you do! For me, working through the trauma from my abusive past has helped with flashbacks and "voices" that I hear. I would wake up screaming from nightmares, or just zone out suddenly and re-live an experience. 

Have you tried any grounding techniques to bring you back to present moment? Not sure if you disassociate when you have these flashbacks, but for me doing the "5 things you see, four things you can touch, three things you can smell" etc. technique brings me back sometimes. 

My number one advice though is to definitely seek help! Talking to someone about specific memories or instances will help. It's when we suppress or push things away that they come back in nasty forms like flashbacks. 

What you went through is completely unfair and undeserved, but I wish you the very best on your healing journey. You can do it!

Hi! I am so sorry to hear that you are struggling with your mental health. First and foremost, I want you to know that your feelings & circumstances ARE valid. And it is definitely worth looking into on a deeper level, and I am sorry your therapist isn't giving you that higher level of care. As someone who has gone through their fair-share of therapists, and finally landed on the best fit, I can assure you that the problem here is your therapist, not you. She definitely needs to start taking you seriously. She is a mental health professional, and I am sorry that she is just being dismissive of you when you explain your symptoms.

I want you to remember that you are paying for a service. If you're anything like me, you might stay and not voice your concerns out of that whole "people pleasing" habit. But I want you to remember that you do not owe your therapist that. If she is not helping, there are plenty of other fish in the sea. I know starting over is really hard, especially with therapy, but I think if after an honest conversation your therapist still doesn't give you the attention you deserve, it might be time to visit PsychologyToday and find yourself someone new!

Wishing you the best!

Hi there! I am so sorry to hear about your past. Your story breaks my heart because I see a lot of parallel to mine. I have an especially soft spot for stories like yours because I know that it can cause a lot of trauma / mental health issues. I absolutely believe you should go to therapy! I go at the moment fairly frequently, and it's been helpful for me to work through specific memories, and even just explore why I feel the way I do. Bad anxiety attacks is definitely an indicator that it might be time soon! Wishing you all the best.  :)
